Installing a Macro in Another Workbook
Should you prefer to create the report first and then add the macros, then proceed as follows.
On the Excel menu lick Tools then Macro then Visual Basic Editor.
From the Visual Basic menu select View Project Explorer you will see VBA Project (your workbook name)
Click + opposite Modules for each to view the modules attached to each file; your workbook may or
may not already have modules.  Note that you will need the macro password (from your supervisor).
The master_report_2003.xls project has five Modules ; 'Add_Pages', 'Auto_PDF_Print',
Drag the required Module across to your workbook project and drop it into the Modules folder, if there is
one, otherwise into the Microsoft Excel Objects folder.
Return to master_report_2003.xls in Excel and right mouse button click on the appropriate button required

Subject : Water Analysis, DLD-32L Well
                Our Ref: MFL 20130041

Two (2) bottomhole water samples were collected from DLD-32L well and forwarded to our Kuala Lumpur laboratory for water analysis.

Samples Received
Two (2) bottomhole water samples were collected from DLD-32L well and forwarded to our Kuala Lumpur laboratory for API 12 ion Water Analysis, Salinity, Resistivity, pH, Specific Gravity, Total Dissolved Solids and Scaling Potential analyses.

Gas-Water Ratio by Flash Separation Technique
A known volume of the bottomhole water sample was flashed to atmospheric pressure and laboratory temperature (20°C). The dissolved gas from the bottomhole water sample was collected  by using flash/separation technique.The dissolved gas was then analysed through extended gas analysis technique.  Utilizing the volumetric data from the flash/separation technique, Gas-Water-Ratio (GWR) was calculated. The schematic diagram of flash separation technique is presented as Figure 1 on page A.3 of this report. After completion of the flash process for GWR, the balance of bottomhole water sample was flashed to atmospheric and collected as stocktank water for further water analysis.

Water Compositional Analysis
Salinity
Conductivity and salinity measures waters ability to conduct electricity, which provides a measure of what is dissolved in water. Salinity is estimated from conductivity measurement. Since salts in water conduct current, conductivity is proportional to the salt-concentration. A complex mathematical equation is utilized to calculate or estimate salinity from conductivity. This equation accounts for the temperature dependence of conductivity.

Elemental Analysis 
The sample was filtered through a Whatman No. 5 filter paper and a dilution was made, using distilled water, according to their salinity. This is to ensure that all the elements are in the correct range for ICP analysis.  The result was presented in mg/l on the ICP (Inductively Coupled Plasma Atomic Emission Spectroscopy) for all detectable elements found in formation waters, seawaters and drilling fluids. A routine water analysis consists of determining the following ions by ICP technique – sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, barium, strontium, dissolved iron, sulphate (as total sulphur), phosphorus, silicon, boron, aluminium and lithium.

Chloride Content
The diluted sample was then analysed for chloride content by titration with silver nitrate solution using an ion selective electrode. Before usage, the instrument was calibrated by running a quality control sample.

pH / Bicarbonate / Carbonate Determinations
pH and bicarbonate determinations were performed by ion selective electrode. The instrument was first calibrated using pH 10, 7 and 4 buffers and checked by using a bicarbonate quality control sample. The pH and bicarbonate determinations was performed on filtered undiluted sample. The pH of a sample was initially determined using an ion selective electrode.  If pH is above 8.1, the sample is titrated with sulphuric acid for carbonate down to pH 8.1 then down to pH 4.1 for bicarbonate.

Total Iron Determinations
The measurement was performed on unfiltered & undiluted sample.  A 10ml aliquot of water was sub-sampled and heated on a hotplate after the addition of hydrochloric acid.  The sample was filtered into a 100 ml flask and made up to the mark with distilled water (x 10 dilution). The sample was then read on the ICP for total iron concentration.

Specific Gravity & Density
This analysis was performed using a density meter on a filtered & undiluted sample. The temperature was set at 15.6°C and the specific gravity was reported at 60°F.

Resistivity Determinations
The  resistivity determination was performed on filtered & undiluted sample using a null point method and noting the temperature reading.  The resistivity was reported as a calculated value at 60°F.

Gas Compositions
Gas compositions were determined using extended gas chromatography by the GPA 2286 method using a multi-column gas chromatograph system.  A single partial pressure charge was passed through the sampling valve and charged to each analytical column. The TCD (Thermal Conductivity Detector) reads O2, N2 and C1 from the molecular sieve column followed by C2, CO2, C3, iC4, nC4, iC5, nC5 from the porous polymer column. The FID (Flame Ionization Detector) reads up to Cn+ from the capillary column independently. A temperature programme was used in order to provide optimum detection and resolution of the dodecanes plus components.

Notes:
Sulphate results are calculated from total sulphur determined by inductively coupled plasma emission spectrometry.

Notes:
Sulphate results are calculated from total sulphur determined by inductively coupled plasma emission spectrometry.

Note :
The residue mole weight and density values ( eg heptanes plus, undecanes plus, eicosanes plus) are calculated so that the calculated average mole weights and densities correspond with the measured values. This can lead to anomalous residue mole weights and densities where the Katz and Firoozabadi values may not be suitable for the isomer groups detected.

Note :
The gas mole % compositions were calculated from the measured weight % compositions using the most detailed analysis results, involving as many of the above components as were identified.  The reported component mole % compositions were then sub-grouped into the generic carbon number components.
